summary.headline: Bansal Wire Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 25% YoY to INR 1,168 crore, with EBITDA of INR 57 crore and PAT of INR 20 crore after a gas-driven margin hit.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was hit in its first 45 days by a spike in gas and consumable costs (about INR 5,000 a tonne blended) linked to West Asia tensions, and management chose to absorb the cost on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders, cutting blended EBITDA to about INR 2 a kg. Margins recovered to about INR 7-8 a kg from around May 15, and management says operations are back to normal levels. Sales volume was 112,000 tonnes versus 104,000 tonnes a year earlier, and operating cash flow was about INR 121 crore. Management reiterated 20% volume and EBITDA growth for the rest of FY27 and kept capex at INR 200-250 crore a year.

financial_highlights.value: about INR 4-4.5 a kg for the quarter
financial_highlights.change: first 45 days about INR 2 a kg; later period INR 7-8 a kg

segments.name: Core B2B wire business
segments.commentary: Absorbed a cost shock on about 30-40 days of firm-price orders; new orders were priced at INR 8 a kg blended. Management says volume growth lagged its 20% target because of a demand dip and customer destocking.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry steel wire)
segments.commentary: Launched in the quarter and contributed about 10% of sales. Management targets B2C at 25% of total sales, which is 50% of the low-carbon business, and says B2C EBITDA per tonne is 20-30% above B2B low-carbon.

segments.name: Speciality wires (IHT, OHT, Steel Cord)
segments.commentary: IHT capacity is 9,000 tonnes, rising to 15,000 tonnes with OHT by year-end. IHT utilisation is at 35-40% and targeted at about 50% next month. Steel Cord has a 20,000-tonne pilot and received its first trial order from a leading Indian tire maker; four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% for the rest of FY27, with EBITDA growth guided at a similar 20% or more.
EBITDA per kg is expected to stay around INR 7-8 a kg after the Q1 disruption.
Capex capped at INR 200-250 crore a year, including FY27; IHT and OHT utilisation targeted at 60-80% by year-end.
Speciality target of about INR 2 lakh tonnes of capacity, with EBITDA of INR 600-800 crore on INR 2,000-2,500 crore of investment (per management's math).
Target of 25% ROCE in the current business over a short period.
Operating cash flow target of INR 350 crore for FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity is about 680,000 tonnes; FY27 started with 680,000 tonnes plus 60,000 tonnes that can be commissioned as needed.
Management aims to start each year with 20-25% spare capacity and historically runs at 85-90% utilisation.
Sanand facility wire expansion of about 90,000 tonnes is under way; some surplus land there may be sold in part.
Dadri greenfield facility had early hiccups that management says are resolved, and ramp-up is now under way.
OHT wire is expected to commission shortly and be fully operational by year-end.
demand_pricing: Demand is recovering across most sectors, including exports and automotive; management says 2Q and 3Q are seasonally weaker in infra.
Management says the industry grows 7-8% while Bansal has grown about 20% a year over the last two decades.
Speciality: India is 60-65% imported and Bansal targets 45-50% share of that market at full capacity; export is not seen as viable because of raw material cost gaps of INR 10-15 a kg.
IHT EBITDA is about INR 10-20 a kg at optimum utilisation, with 80% of customers already approving the product.
Gas costs rose about 1.5x on a blended basis and had not come down as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and growth hold if the geopolitical and oil-price issue persists for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management absorbed about INR 5,000 a tonne of consumable cost on firm-price orders for the first 45 days, which took EBITDA down to about INR 2 a kg. Margins have been back at INR 7-8 a kg since about May 15.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company run a cost-plus model, and why did the quarter's margin fall so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is cost-plus, but about 30-40 days of inventory was tied to fixed-rate orders, so the cost rise hit immediately. New orders were booked at escalated prices from April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book from the first Steel Cord trial customer and when will a firm order come?
qa_highlights.answer: It is only a trial order with no firm order book yet. Four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months, so a firm order could take six to eight months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CFO guidance rise to about INR 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 from about INR 600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 600 crore figure was a combined two-year target. FY26 delivered about INR 330 crore against a INR 250 crore target, and FY27's target is INR 350 crore, with INR 115 crore already generated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IHT and OHT margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: IHT is at 35-40% utilisation, targeting about 50% next month. Break-even is at about 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70-80%. Combined IHT and OHT EBITDA is expected at INR 10-20 a kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is capped at INR 200-250 crore a year to support 20-25% volume growth. Management said there will be no unusually high capex year apart from Speciality.

risks_watch: Gas and consumable costs had not eased by the call, and a reversal could create inventory losses on the 30-40 days of stock held at cost.
Volume growth must reach about 145,000 tonnes a quarter over the next three quarters, which implies roughly 85% utilisation.
Receivable and payable days: the company used payables financing and vendor advances, and management plans to cut receivable days.
Speciality ROCE depends on the Steel Cord ramp, which is still in trial stages with no firm order book.
Sanand land: management clarified that the land is not being sold outright, which resolves the earlier confusion over asset-held-for-sale presentation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on recovery and growth, with management saying the fundamental challenges are almost over. Management was cautious on Speciality timelines and on pricing, noting "a lot of uncertainty is still remaining" and that Steel Cord is still a long process.
key_quotes: Now as of today, even with all of this crisis today, we see that the demand is there.
We are operating at regular EBITDA with an escalated cost.
Once we reach an optimum capacity utilization, I would say that we can expect similar EBITDA, like we are thinking of Steel Cord or something like that in percentage.
We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year.

adds.what: Speciality OHT wire capacity lifting IHT/OHT total to 15,000 tonnes
Sanand facility wire expansion of about 90,000 tonnes
Dadri greenfield facility ramp-up under way after early hiccups

growth.why: Management reiterated 20% volume growth for the rest of FY27 and at least 20% EBITDA growth, backed partly by the 90,000 t Sanand expansion, OHT ramp to 15,000 t by year-end, Steel Cord trials and a B2C launch; order-level specifics were not quantified, and volume lagged target in Q1 due to destocking.
